sanskrit: yuddheṣv apavadiṣyanti yodhā nūnaṃ vṛkodaram yāvat sthāsyanti bhūtāni nikṛtyā hy asi pātitaḥ
english: In their battles warriors will surely speak ill of Vṛkodara for as long as living beings endure, for by foul treachery you were brought down.

sanskrit: nanu rāmo 'bravīd rājaṃs tvāṃ sadā yadunandanaḥ duryodhanasamo nāsti gadayā iti vīryavān
english: Did not Rāma, the valiant scion of the Yadus, ever say of you, O king, that there is none equal to Duryodhana with the mace?

sanskrit: ślāghate tvāṃ hi vārṣṇeyo rājan saṃsatsu bhārata suśiṣyo mama kauravyo gadāyuddha iti prabho
english: For the Vārṣṇeya praised you in the assemblies, O king, O Bhārata, saying, 'The Kaurava is my fine pupil in the fighting of maces,' O lord.

sanskrit: yāṃ gatiṃ kṣatriyasyāhuḥ praśastāṃ paramarṣayaḥ hatasyābhimukhasyājau prāptas tvam asi tāṃ gatim
english: The destiny that the supreme sages declare blessed for a kṣatriya — that of one slain facing the foe in battle — that destiny you have attained.

sanskrit: duryodhana na śocāmi tvām ahaṃ puruṣarṣabha hataputrāṃ tu śocāmi gāndhārīṃ pitaraṃ ca te bhikṣukau vicariṣyete śocantau pṛthivīm imām
english: Duryodhana, I do not grieve for you, O bull among men; but I grieve for Gāndhārī, bereft of her sons, and for your father — those two will wander this earth as beggars, mourning.

sanskrit: dhig astu kṛṣṇaṃ vārṣṇeyam arjunaṃ cāpi durmatim dharmajñamāninau yau tvāṃ vadhyamānam upekṣatām
english: A curse upon Kṛṣṇa the Vārṣṇeya, and upon the wicked-minded Arjuna too — those two, who fancy themselves knowers of dharma, yet looked on while you were being struck down.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś cāpi te sarve kiṃ vakṣyanti narādhipān kathaṃ duryodhano 'smābhir hata ity anapatrapāḥ
english: And what will all those Pāṇḍavas say to the kings — those shameless ones — about how Duryodhana was slain by us?

sanskrit: dhanyas tvam asi gāndhāre yas tvam āyodhane hataḥ prayāto 'bhimukhaḥ śatrūn dharmeṇa puruṣarṣabha
english: Fortunate are you, son of Gāndhārī, who were slain upon the field of battle, having gone forth to face your foes by the way of dharma, O bull among men.

sanskrit: hataputrā hi gāndhārī nihatajñātibāndhavā prajñācakṣuś ca durdharṣaḥ kāṃ gatiṃ pratipatsyate
english: For Gāndhārī, her sons slain, her kinsmen and kindred destroyed, and the unassailable one whose sight is wisdom — what destiny shall they meet?

sanskrit: dhig astu kṛtavarmāṇaṃ māṃ kṛpaṃ ca mahāratham ye vayaṃ na gatāḥ svargaṃ tvāṃ puraskṛtya pārthivam
english: A curse upon Kṛtavarman, upon me, and upon Kṛpa the great chariot-warrior — we who have not gone to heaven setting you, O king, before us.

sanskrit: dātāraṃ sarvakāmānāṃ rakṣitāraṃ prajāhitam yad vayaṃ nānugacchāmas tvāṃ dhig asmān narādhamān
english: You who gave us all our desires, who guarded us, who sought the welfare of your people — that we do not follow you, a curse upon us, basest of men.

sanskrit: kṛpasya tava vīryeṇa mama caiva pituś ca me sabhṛtyānāṃ naravyāghra ratnavanti gṛhāṇi ca
english: By your might, O tiger among men, the houses of Kṛpa, of me, and of my father, together with our retainers, were filled with jewels.

sanskrit: bhavatprasādād asmābhiḥ samitraiḥ sahabāndhavaiḥ avāptāḥ kratavo mukhyā bahavo bhūridakṣiṇāḥ
english: By your grace, we with our friends and kinsmen performed many great sacrifices with lavish gifts to the priests.

sanskrit: kutaś cāpīdṛśaṃ sārtham upalapsyāmahe vayam yādṛśena puraskṛtya tvaṃ gataḥ sarvapārthivān
english: And where shall we ever find such a companion, with whom set before you, you departed surpassing all the kings of the earth?

sanskrit: vayam eva trayo rājan gacchantaṃ paramāṃ gatim yad vai tvāṃ nānugacchāmas tena tapsyāmahe vayam
english: We three alone, O king, since we do not follow you as you go to the supreme destiny — for that we shall burn with remorse.

sanskrit: tvatsvargahīnā hīnārthāḥ smarantaḥ sukṛtasya te kiṃ nāma tad bhavet karma yena tvānuvrajema vai
english: Bereft of your heaven, bereft of our purpose, remembering your good deeds — what deed could there be by which we might follow after you?

sanskrit: duḥkhaṃ nūnaṃ kuruśreṣṭha cariṣyāmo mahīm imām hīnānāṃ nas tvayā rājan kutaḥ śāntiḥ kutaḥ sukham
english: In sorrow, surely, O best of the Kurus, shall we roam this earth; for us bereft of you, O king, whence peace, whence happiness?

sanskrit: gatvaitāṃs tu mahārāja sametya tvaṃ mahārathān yathāśreṣṭhaṃ yathājyeṣṭhaṃ pūjayer vacanān mama
english: Having gone, O great king, and met those great chariot-warriors, you should honor them, each by his rank and seniority, in my name.

sanskrit: ācāryaṃ pūjayitvā ca ketuṃ sarvadhanuṣmatām hataṃ mayādya śaṃsethā dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ narādhipa
english: And having honored the teacher, the banner of all bowmen, you should tell him, O king, that Dhṛṣṭadyumna was slain by me this day.

sanskrit: pariṣvajethā rājānaṃ bāhlikaṃ sumahāratham saindhavaṃ somadattaṃ ca bhūriśravasam eva ca
english: You should embrace King Bāhlika, the mighty chariot-warrior, and the lord of Sindhu, and Somadatta, and Bhūriśravas too.

sanskrit: tathā pūrvagatān anyān svargaṃ pārthivasattamān asmad vākyāt pariṣvajya pṛcchethās tvam anāmayam
english: And so too the other best of kings who have gone before to heaven — embracing them in our name, you should ask after their well-being.

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā rājānaṃ bhagnasaktham acetasam aśvatthāmā samudvīkṣya punar vacanam abravīt
english: Having thus spoken to the king, his thighs shattered and his senses gone, Aśvatthāman, gazing upon him, spoke once more.

sanskrit: duryodhana jīvasi ced vācaṃ śrotrasukhāṃ śṛṇu sapta pāṇḍavataḥ śeṣā dhārtarāṣṭrās trayo vayam
english: Duryodhana, if you yet live, hear words that will be sweet to your ears: of the Pāṇḍavas seven remain; of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's side, we three.

sanskrit: te caiva bhrātaraḥ pañca vāsudevo 'tha sātyakiḥ ahaṃ ca kṛtavarmā ca kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tathā
english: They are the five brothers, then Vāsudeva and Sātyaki; and on our side I, and Kṛtavarman, and Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat.

sanskrit: draupadeyā hatāḥ sarve dhṛṣṭadyumnasya cātmajāḥ pāñcālā nihatāḥ sarve matsyaśeṣaṃ ca bhārata
english: The sons of Draupadī are all slain, and the sons of Dhṛṣṭadyumna; the Pāñcālas are all destroyed, and what remained of the Matsyas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kṛte pratikṛtaṃ paśya hataputrā hi pāṇḍavāḥ sauptike śibiraṃ teṣāṃ hataṃ sanaravāhanam
english: See the deed repaid with a deed: the Pāṇḍavas too are bereft of their sons; in the night-attack their camp was destroyed, with its men and mounts.

sanskrit: mayā ca pāpakarmāsau dhṛṣṭadyumno mahīpate praviśya śibiraṃ rātrau paśumāreṇa māritaḥ
english: And that evildoer Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O lord of the earth, was killed by me — entering the camp by night, I slaughtered him like a beast.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu tāṃ vācaṃ niśamya manasaḥ priyām pratilabhya punaś ceta idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: But Duryodhana, hearing those words dear to his heart, and recovering his senses once again, spoke this speech.

sanskrit: na me 'karot tad gāṅgeyo na karṇo na ca te pitā yat tvayā kṛpabhojābhyāṃ sahitenādya me kṛtam
english: What you, joined with Kṛpa and the Bhoja, have done for me this day, the son of Gaṅgā did not do for me, nor Karṇa, nor your father.

sanskrit: sa cet senāpatiḥ kṣudro hataḥ sārdhaṃ śikhaṇḍinā tena manye maghavatā samam ātmānam adya vai
english: If that base commander has been slain together with Śikhaṇḍin, then I deem myself this day the equal of Maghavat himself.

sanskrit: svasti prāpnuta bhadraṃ vaḥ svarge naḥ saṃgamaḥ punaḥ ity evam uktvā tūṣṇīṃ sa kururājo mahāmanāḥ prāṇān udasṛjad vīraḥ suhṛdāṃ śokam ādadhat
english: Fare you well, blessings be upon you; in heaven shall be our meeting again. Having spoken thus, the high-minded king of the Kurus fell silent, and the hero gave up his life, leaving sorrow upon his friends.

sanskrit: tatheti te pariṣvaktāḥ pariṣvajya ca taṃ nṛpam punaḥ punaḥ prekṣamāṇāḥ svakān āruruhū rathān
english: Saying 'So be it,' those who had been embraced, embracing the king in turn and gazing upon him again and again, mounted their own chariots.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ tava putrasya niśamya karuṇāṃ giram pratyūṣakāle śokārtaḥ prādhāvaṃ nagaraṃ prati
english: Having thus heard your son's piteous words, at the hour of dawn, stricken with grief, I sped toward the city.

sanskrit: tava putre gate svargaṃ śokārtasya mamānagha ṛṣidattaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ tad divyadarśitvam adya vai
english: When your son had gone to heaven, O blameless one, for me in my grief that gift of the sage, the power of divine sight, was this day lost.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca iti śrutvā sa nṛpatiḥ putrajñātivadhaṃ tadā niḥśvasya dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca tataś cintāparo 'bhavat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard thus of the slaughter of his sons and kinsmen, the king then drew a long, hot sigh and was lost in brooding thought.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnasya sārathiḥ śaśaṃsa dharmarājāya sauptike kadanaṃ kṛtam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When that night had passed, the charioteer of Dhṛṣṭadyumna reported to the King of Dharma the carnage that had been wrought in the night-attack.

sanskrit: draupadeyā mahārāja drupadasyātmajaiḥ saha pramattā niśi viśvastāḥ svapantaḥ śibire svake
english: The sons of Draupadī, O great king, together with the sons of Drupada — heedless, trusting, asleep in their own camp at night —

sanskrit: kṛtavarmaṇā nṛśaṃsena gautamena kṛpeṇa ca aśvatthāmnā ca pāpena hataṃ vaḥ śibiraṃ niśi
english: by the cruel Kṛtavarman, by Kṛpa of Gautama's line, and by the wicked Aśvatthāman — your camp was destroyed in the night.

sanskrit: etair naragajāśvānāṃ prāsaśaktiparaśvadhaiḥ sahasrāṇi nikṛntadbhir niḥśeṣaṃ te balaṃ kṛtam
english: By these men, hacking down thousands of warriors, elephants, and horses with javelins, spears, and battle-axes, your army was utterly annihilated.

sanskrit: chidyamānasya mahato vanasyeva paraśvadhaiḥ śuśruve sumahāñ śabdo balasya tava bhārata
english: Like a great forest being felled with axes, a tremendous din arose from your army, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: aham eko 'vaśiṣṭas tu tasmāt sainyān mahīpate muktaḥ kathaṃ cid dharmātman vyagrasya kṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: I alone am left of that host, O lord of the earth; somehow, O righteous one, I escaped while Kṛtavarman was distracted.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vākyam aśivaṃ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ papāta mahyāṃ durdharṣaḥ putraśokasamanvitaḥ
english: Hearing that grievous report, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī, the unassailable, fell to the ground, overcome with grief for his sons.

sanskrit: taṃ patantam abhikramya parijagrāha sātyakiḥ bhīmaseno 'rjunaś caiva mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: As he fell, Sātyaki rushed forward and caught hold of him, as did Bhīmasena and Arjuna and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: labdhacetās tu kaunteyaḥ śokavihvalayā girā jitvā śatrūñ jitaḥ paścāt paryadevayad āturaḥ
english: Regaining his senses, the son of Kuntī, in a voice broken with grief, having conquered his foes yet conquered after all, lamented in his anguish.

sanskrit: durvidā gatir arthānām api ye divyacakṣuṣaḥ jīyamānā jayanty anye jayamānā vayaṃ jitāḥ
english: Hard to know is the course of events, even for those with divine sight: others, being defeated, prove victorious, while we, prevailing, are defeated.

sanskrit: hatvā bhrātṝn vayasyāṃś ca pitṝn putrān suhṛdgaṇān bandhūn amātyān pautrāṃś ca jitvā sarvāñ jitā vayam
english: Having slain brothers and companions, fathers, sons, and bands of friends, kinsmen, counselors, and grandsons — having conquered them all, we are conquered.

sanskrit: anartho hy arthasaṃkāśas tathārtho 'narthadarśanaḥ jayo 'yam ajayākāro jayas tasmāt parājayaḥ
english: For ruin has the look of gain, and gain the appearance of ruin; this victory has the form of defeat — this victory, therefore, is a defeat.

sanskrit: yaṃ jitvā tapyate paścād āpanna iva durmatiḥ kathaṃ manyeta vijayaṃ tato jitataraḥ paraiḥ
english: When one, having conquered, afterward burns with remorse like a fool fallen into misfortune, how could he account it a victory? — he is rather the more thoroughly vanquished by his foes.

sanskrit: yeṣām arthāya pāpasya dhig jayasya suhṛdvadhe nirjitair apramattair hi vijitā jitakāśinaḥ
english: For the sake of whom — a curse upon this evil victory bought with the slaughter of friends! — those who seemed victorious have in truth been vanquished by the heedful ones they had defeated.

sanskrit: karṇinālīkadaṃṣṭrasya khaḍgajihvasya saṃyuge cāpavyāttasya raudrasya jyātalasvananādinaḥ
english: Of him whose fangs were barbed and shaftlike arrows, whose tongue was the sword, whose terrible jaws gaped wide as the bow in battle, who roared with the twang of the bowstring against the guard —

sanskrit: kruddhasya narasiṃhasya saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinaḥ ye vyamucyanta karṇasya pramādāt ta ime hatāḥ
english: of that wrathful lion among men, Karṇa, who never fled from battles — those who escaped him have now, through heedlessness, been slain.

sanskrit: rathahradaṃ śaravarṣormimantaṃ; ratnācitaṃ vāhanarājiyuktam śaktyṛṣṭimīnadhvajanāganakraṃ; śarāsanāvartamaheṣuphenam
english: A lake whose chariots were its depths, whose waves were showers of arrows, studded with jewels and ranged with mounts; whose fish were lances and spears, whose crocodiles were elephants beneath the standards, whose whirlpools were bows and whose foam the mighty shafts —

sanskrit: saṃgrāmacandrodayavegavelaṃ; droṇārṇavaṃ jyātalanemighoṣam ye terur uccāvacaśastranaubhis; te rājaputrā nihatāḥ pramādāt
english: that ocean of Droṇa, whose tide swelled with the moonrise of battle, roaring with the twang of bowstring, guard, and chariot-rim — those princes who crossed it in boats of high and low weapons have now been slain through heedlessness.

sanskrit: na hi pramādāt paramo 'sti kaś cid; vadho narāṇām iha jīvaloke pramattam arthā hi naraṃ samantāt; tyajanty anarthāś ca samāviśanti
english: For there is no slayer of men in this world of the living greater than heedlessness; the heedless man fortune abandons on every side, and misfortunes crowd in upon him.

sanskrit: dhvajottamāgrocchritadhūmaketuṃ; śarārciṣaṃ kopamahāsamīram mahādhanurjyātalanemighoṣaṃ; tanutranānāvidhaśastrahomam
english: Whose smoke-bannered fire blazed high atop the topmost standards, whose flames were arrows and whose great wind was wrath, whose roar was of the mighty bow's string, guard, and rim, whose oblations were armor and weapons of every kind —

sanskrit: mahācamūkakṣavarābhipannaṃ; mahāhave bhīṣmamahādavāgnim ye sehur āttāyataśastravegaṃ; te rājaputrā nihatāḥ pramādāt
english: that great forest-fire of Bhīṣma in the mighty fray, fed upon the thicket of great armies — those princes who withstood its onrush of drawn and uplifted weapons have now been slain through heedlessness.

sanskrit: na hi pramattena nareṇa labhyā; vidyā tapaḥ śrīr vipulaṃ yaśo vā paśyāpramādena nihatya śatrūn; sarvān mahendraṃ sukham edhamānam
english: For by a heedless man no learning is won, nor austerity, nor splendor, nor wide renown; behold great Indra, who by heedfulness slew all his foes and now flourishes in happiness.

sanskrit: indropamān pārthivaputrapautrān; paśyāviśeṣeṇa hatān pramādāt tīrtvā samudraṃ vaṇijaḥ samṛddhāḥ; sannāḥ kunadyām iva helamānāḥ amarṣitair ye nihatāḥ śayānā; niḥsaṃśayaṃ te tridivaṃ prapannāḥ
english: Behold the sons and grandsons of kings, the equals of Indra, slain alike through heedlessness — like prosperous merchants who, having crossed the sea, sink heedlessly in a wretched little stream. Those who lay sleeping and were slain by the wrathful ones have, without doubt, attained to heaven.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāṃ nu śocāmi kathaṃ na sādhvīṃ; śokārṇave sādya vinaṅkṣyatīti bhrātṝṃś ca putrāṃś ca hatān niśamya; pāñcālarājaṃ pitaraṃ ca vṛddham dhruvaṃ visaṃjñā patitā pṛthivyāṃ; sā śeṣyate śokakṛśāṅgayaṣṭiḥ
english: How should I not grieve for the virtuous Kṛṣṇā, who now will surely perish, sinking into an ocean of sorrow? Hearing that her brothers and sons are slain, and the aged king of the Pāñcālas, her father, she will surely fall senseless to the earth and lie there, her slender frame wasted with grief.

sanskrit: tac chokajaṃ duḥkham apārayantī; kathaṃ bhaviṣyaty ucitā sukhānām putrakṣayabhrātṛvadhapraṇunnā; pradahyamāneva hutāśanena
english: Unable to bear that grief-born anguish, how shall she fare, she who was accustomed to happiness — driven by the loss of her sons and the slaughter of her brothers, as though consumed by the fire that devours the oblations?

sanskrit: ity evam ārtaḥ paridevayan sa; rājā kurūṇāṃ nakulaṃ babhāṣe gacchānayainām iha mandabhāgyāṃ; samātṛpakṣām iti rājaputrīm
english: Thus, lamenting in his anguish, the king of the Kurus said to Nakula: 'Go and bring here that ill-fated princess, together with her mother's kin.'

sanskrit: mādrīsutas tat parigṛhya vākyaṃ; dharmeṇa dharmapratimasya rājñaḥ yayau rathenālayam āśu devyāḥ; pāñcālarājasya ca yatra dārāḥ
english: Receiving that command of the king, who was dharma's very image, the son of Mādrī swiftly went by chariot to the queen's abode, where the wives of the Pāñcāla king dwelt.

sanskrit: prasthāpya mādrīsutam ājamīḍhaḥ; śokārditas taiḥ sahitaḥ suhṛdbhiḥ rorūyamāṇaḥ prayayau sutānām; āyodhanaṃ bhūtagaṇānukīrṇam
english: Having sent off the son of Mādrī, the descendant of Ajamīḍha, tormented by grief and accompanied by his friends, set out, weeping aloud, for the battleground of his sons, thronged with crowds of spirits.

sanskrit: sa tat praviśyāśivam ugrarūpaṃ; dadarśa putrān suhṛdaḥ sakhīṃś ca bhūmau śayānān rudhirārdragātrān; vibhinnabhagnāpahṛtottamāṅgān
english: Entering that dreadful, fearsome place, he beheld his sons, his kinsmen, and his friends lying upon the ground, their limbs drenched in blood, their heads split, broken off, and carried away.

sanskrit: sa tāṃs tu dṛṣṭvā bhṛśam ārtarūpo; yudhiṣṭhiro dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ uccaiḥ pracukrośa ca kauravāgryaḥ; papāta corvyāṃ sagaṇo visaṃjñaḥ
english: Beholding them, Yudhiṣṭhira, the foremost of dharma's upholders, deeply stricken, the chief of the Kurus, cried out aloud and fell to the earth senseless, together with his company.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa dṛṣṭvā nihatān saṃkhye putrān bhrātṝn sakhīṃs tathā mahāduḥkhaparītātmā babhūva janamejaya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Beholding his sons, brothers, and friends slain in battle, his soul was overwhelmed with great anguish, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: tatas tasya mahāñ śokaḥ prādurāsīn mahātmanaḥ smarataḥ putrapautrāṇāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ svajanasya ha
english: Then a great grief arose in that high-souled one as he remembered his sons and grandsons, his brothers, and his own people.

sanskrit: tam aśruparipūrṇākṣaṃ vepamānam acetasam suhṛdo bhṛśasaṃvignāḥ sāntvayāṃ cakrire tadā
english: His eyes brimming with tears, trembling and bereft of his senses, his deeply distressed friends then sought to console him.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin kṣaṇe kālye rathenādityavarcasā nakulaḥ kṛṣṇayā sārdham upāyāt paramārtayā
english: Then at that morning hour, in a chariot bright as the sun, Nakula arrived together with Kṛṣṇā, who was utterly overcome with grief.

sanskrit: upaplavyagatā sā tu śrutvā sumahad apriyam tadā vināśaṃ putrāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ vyathitābhavat
english: She, who had been at Upaplavya, on hearing that most grievous news — the destruction of all her sons — was then stricken with anguish.

sanskrit: kampamāneva kadalī vātenābhisamīritā kṛṣṇā rājānam āsādya śokārtā nyapatad bhuvi
english: Trembling like a plantain shaken by the wind, Kṛṣṇā, reaching the king and stricken with grief, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: babhūva vadanaṃ tasyāḥ sahasā śokakarśitam phullapadmapalāśākṣyās tamodhvasta ivāṃśumān
english: The face of her whose eyes were like the petals of a full-blown lotus grew suddenly wasted with grief, like the sun overcast by darkness.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃrambhī satyavikramaḥ bāhubhyāṃ parijagrāha samupetya vṛkodaraḥ
english: Then, seeing her fallen, the impetuous Vṛkodara of true valor came up and caught her in his arms.

sanskrit: sā samāśvāsitā tena bhīmasenena bhāminī rudatī pāṇḍavaṃ kṛṣṇā sahabhrātaram abravīt
english: Comforted by Bhīmasena, the beautiful Kṛṣṇā, weeping, spoke to the Pāṇḍava and his brothers.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā rājaṃs tvam adyemām akhilāṃ bhokṣyase mahīm ātmajān kṣatradharmeṇa saṃpradāya yamāya vai
english: By fortune, O king, you shall this day enjoy this whole earth, having delivered up your sons to Yama by the law of the kṣatriya.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tvaṃ pārtha kuśalī mattamātaṅgagāminam avāpya pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ saubhadraṃ na smariṣyasi
english: By fortune, O Pārtha, you are safe and well; having gained the whole earth, you will not remember the son of Subhadrā, who walked with the gait of a rutting elephant.

sanskrit: ātmajāṃs tena dharmeṇa śrutvā śūrān nipātitān upaplavye mayā sārdhaṃ diṣṭyā tvaṃ na smariṣyasi
english: Having heard that your valiant sons were struck down by that law of war, by fortune you will not remember them — those who dwelt with me at Upaplavya.

sanskrit: prasuptānāṃ vadhaṃ śrutvā drauṇinā pāpakarmaṇā śokas tapati māṃ pārtha hutāśana ivāśayam
english: Hearing of the slaughter of the sleeping by the evil-deeded son of Droṇa, grief scorches me, O Pārtha, like fire consuming my heart.

sanskrit: tasya pāpakṛto drauṇer na ced adya tvayā mṛdhe hriyate sānubandhasya yudhi vikramya jīvitam
english: If this day, in battle, you do not by your valor take the life of that wicked son of Droṇa, together with his followers,

sanskrit: ihaiva prāyam āsiṣye tan nibodhata pāṇḍavāḥ na cet phalam avāpnoti drauṇiḥ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ
english: then here and now I shall sit fasting unto death — mark this well, O Pāṇḍavas — unless the son of Droṇa reaps the fruit of his evil deed.
